Adding a lens

Source: vignettes/adding-a-lens.Rmd
adding-a-lens.Rmd
library(quorum)

Why

A colleague has just produced a second fit of the same mixed model, this time from glmmTMB’s Laplace approximation rather than the hub’s INLA backend. Before the two can stand side by side in a quorum, each has to say what it shares with the other and what it does not – otherwise “the two lenses agree” could mean nothing more than “the two lenses share a sampler”. This vignette builds that declaration from the ground up: what a lens must say about itself, how much two lenses actually share once they say it, and how far apart their posteriors sit once the sharing is accounted for.

What

A quorum_lens() (built with lens()) is a member’s fitter behind three declarations. shares names what the lens has in common with every other lens across four components – sampler, objective, priors and data_prep – and is what quorum_independence() reads to weigh an agreement. expresses names the response shapes the lens can represent (linear, plateau, threshold, nonmonotone). scope is a gate: a function of the specification that returns TRUE inside the lens’s corner and a quorum_abstention() outside it, so a model the lens cannot field is declined rather than mis-fitted. Its fit(spec, data, ...) returns a quorum_draws() – a named list of numeric draws, one vector per parameter, for a lens of kind "parameters" – or a quorum_abstention() when it cannot answer this particular model. agreement_pairwise() compares two lenses’ draws component by component; quorum() is the front door that gates, fits, compares and resolves a whole quorum of lenses at once.

Do

Engines available on this build

Two of this vignette’s sections need an optional engine each: lens_tmb() needs glmmTMB and tmbstan, and the hub comparison needs INLA through flexyBayes::flexybayes(). Each guarded chunk below checks for its own engine and prints one sentence in its place when the engine is absent, so the vignette still renders – with less to read – on a build that carries neither.

has_tmb <- requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("tmbstan", quietly = TRUE)
has_inla <- requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
engines_ok <- has_tmb && has_inla

A tiny synthetic toy

A synthetic Gaussian random-intercept toy: 60 observations in 6 groups, an intercept of 2, and a group-level SD of 0.8, seeded for reproducibility. Real data would work the same way; the toy exists only to keep both fits fast.

set.seed(20260902)
n <- 60L
n_groups <- 6L
g <- factor(rep(seq_len(n_groups), each = n / n_groups))
u <- rnorm(n_groups, 0, 0.8)
data_toy <- data.frame(y = 2 + u[as.integer(g)] + rnorm(n, 0, 1), g = g)
head(data_toy)
#>          y g
#> 1 4.027361 1
#> 2 4.263503 1
#> 3 0.769172 1
#> 4 2.880675 1
#> 5 1.499465 1
#> 6 2.118333 1

A worked TMB lens

lens_tmb() fits glmmTMB’s Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood and then samples the very TMB objective that fit produced with tmbstan’s NUTS sampler – a second Laplace family distinct from INLA’s, and one objective sampled two ways. The call below keeps the chain count and iteration count small, which is enough for a toy this size and is exactly what keeps this vignette fast.

tmb_lens <- lens_tmb(chains = 2L, iter = 1000L)
tmb_draws <- tmb_lens@fit(y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data_toy)
#> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess
tmb_draws@source
#> [1] "glmmTMB+tmbstan"
names(tmb_draws@draws)
#> [1] "(Intercept)" "sd_g"

A second lens from the hub

lens_from_fit() wraps a model somebody has already fitted – here, the hub’s own INLA backend on the identical formula – and canonicalises its draws onto the same parameter names the TMB lens uses, so the two are comparable component by component with no relabelling step.

withr::local_options(list(flexyBayes.silence_default_prior_note = TRUE))
hub_fit <- flexyBayes::flexybayes(
  y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data = data_toy, backend = "inla", verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 1L
)
#> flexyBayes: `seed` is a Stan sampler setting the INLA backend does not use, so it has no effect on this fit. INLA's nested Laplace approximation draws no random numbers, so `seed` cannot pin a fit. On a well-identified model two runs agree because the optimiser does. On a weakly identified variance component the landing point can move, so treat that the same way as a failed sampler diagnostic, not as something a seed would fix.
hub_lens <- lens_from_fit(hub_fit, name = "inla")
if (is_quorum_abstention(hub_lens)) {
  # a lens that cannot hand over its draws declines, typed, and the rest of
  # the comparison is skipped rather than run against nothing
  print(hub_lens)
  engines_ok <- FALSE
} else {
  hub_draws <- hub_lens@fit(NULL, NULL)
  names(hub_draws@draws)
}
#> [1] "(Intercept)" "sigma"       "sd_g"

How much the two lenses actually share 

ind <- quorum_independence(list(tmb_lens, hub_lens))
ind
#> <quorum independence ledger>
#>   components: sampler, objective, priors, data_prep
#>   evidential weight (1 = shares nothing, 0 = shares everything)
#>      tmb inla
#> tmb   NA    1
#> inla   1   NA
#>   data independence: NA
#>   Agreement between lenses fitted to the same data is agreement, not corroboration of a shared data fact.
Evidential weight between the TMB and INLA lenses (1 = shares nothing, 0 = shares everything).
tmb inla
tmb NA 1
inla 1 NA

Both lenses declare every one of the four components differently – a Laplace sampler against Stan’s NUTS, the TMB objective against INLA’s own, a hub-matched gamma prior against INLA’s default fixed-effect prior as the hub applies it, and quorum’s own data preparation against the hub’s – so the ledger gives the pair the full evidential weight of 1: nothing about their agreement can be explained by something they share.

How far apart their posteriors sit 

agree <- agreement_pairwise(tmb_draws, hub_draws)
agree
#>         param    mean_a    mean_b      sd_a      sd_b sd_ratio   q025_diff
#> 1 (Intercept) 1.9546004 1.9299431 0.3558124 0.3173628 1.121153 -0.07783524
#> 2        sd_g 0.6845251 0.6602964 0.4439164 0.3786347 1.172413 -0.03778684
#>   q975_diff wasserstein_1 mean_shift_sd     w1_sd    verdict
#> 1 0.1447766    0.03626885    0.06929863 0.1019325 discordant
#> 2 0.3894047    0.08930809    0.05457932 0.2011822 discordant
#>                                 reason
#> 1 Wasserstein-1 0.10 SD; SD ratio 1.12
#> 2 Wasserstein-1 0.20 SD; SD ratio 1.17
Per-component agreement, TMB lens (a) against the hub’s INLA lens (b).
param mean_a mean_b sd_ratio w1_sd verdict
(Intercept) 1.955 1.93 1.121 0.102 discordant
sd_g 0.685 0.66 1.172 0.201 discordant

Figure: the two posteriors, overlaid 

w1_intercept <- agree$w1_sd[agree$param == "(Intercept)"]
overlay_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(value = tmb_draws@draws[["(Intercept)"]], lens = "tmb"),
  data.frame(value = hub_draws@draws[["(Intercept)"]], lens = "inla")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(overlay_df, ggplot2::aes(x = value, fill = lens)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "lens") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "(Intercept)", y = "posterior density",
    title = "Posterior overlay: (Intercept)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Wasserstein-1 distance = %.2f reference SD", w1_intercept
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Posterior density of the intercept under the TMB lens (NUTS over the TMB objective) and the hub’s INLA lens, on the same synthetic toy. The subtitle carries the Wasserstein-1 distance between the two, in reference-SD units, from the agreement table above.

Comparing the two lenses through the front door 

verdict <- quorum(
  list(tmb_lens, hub_lens), spec = y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data = data_toy,
  policy = quorum_policy(order = c("inla", "tmb"), min_lenses = 2L)
)
#> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess
verdict
#> <quorum verdict> status: discordant
#>   lenses: 2 (2 contributing, 0 abstained)
#>   carried: inla (decide) -> no number issued
#>   findings: 0
#>   independence: Agreement between lenses fitted to the same data is agreement, not corroboration of a shared data fact.

Writing your own adapter

A lens needs no engine at all – only a fit() that returns a quorum_draws() or a quorum_abstention(), and the three declarations that say what the estimate is worth alongside another lens’s. The toy below moment-matches a Gaussian to the sample mean of data$y and declares that it shares nothing with any engine-backed lens, because it genuinely does not.

my_fit <- function(spec, data, ...) {
  quorum_draws(
    list(`(Intercept)` = rnorm(200L, mean(data$y), 1)),
    source = "moment_matched"
  )
}
my_lens <- lens(
  name = "toy_moment_match", member = "example", fit = my_fit,
  shares = c(sampler = "none", objective = "moment_matching",
            priors = "none", data_prep = "quorum"),
  expresses = "linear"
)
my_lens@fit(NULL, data_toy)
#> <quorum::quorum_draws>
#>  @ kind       : chr "parameters"
#>  @ draws      :List of 1
#>  .. $ (Intercept): num [1:200] 1.463 1.136 1.447 2.181 0.758 ...
#>  @ grid       : NULL
#>  @ n          : int 200
#>  @ source     : chr "moment_matched"
#>  @ diagnostics: list()

Every built-in lens names its parameter draws on one shared vocabulary, so that any two lenses – however different their engines – line up component by component with no relabelling: "(Intercept)" for the intercept, the model-matrix column name for every other fixed-effect coefficient, "sigma" for the residual standard deviation, and "sd_<group>" for the standard deviation of a random intercept on grouping variable <group>. A new adapter that wants to sit alongside the built-in lenses names its own draws on that same vocabulary; a lens that reports a component under any other name simply will not be found by agreement_pairwise() when it looks for what the two lenses have in common.

Read

On this run the intercept sits 0.1 reference SDs apart under the Wasserstein-1 distance, and the pair’s overall verdict is discordant. The front door carries the inla lens’s answer regardless – quorum() compares lenses, it never prices a decision, so with no decide argument the carried answer is NA and only the comparison itself is reported. Two lenses that share nothing can still disagree: independence is what makes an agreement worth something, not a guarantee that one will be found. The random-intercept SD (sd_g) is the harder component here, which is expected on a toy this small – six groups leave little information for a variance component, and the Laplace approximation underlying the TMB lens is at its least reliable exactly there.

Limits

This toy is synthetic and deliberately small, chosen to keep both samplers fast rather than to stress either engine: six groups is too few to identify a random-intercept SD precisely under any method, which is part of why that component agrees less well than the intercept above. The independence ledger reads only what a lens declares about itself; it cannot discover an undeclared dependency, so a lens that mis-states its own shares will mislead the ledger in a way no computation here can catch. Agreement between two lenses fitted to the same data, as both are here, is agreement about that dataset, not independent corroboration of the fact behind it – the caveat quorum_independence() attaches to every such pair says so explicitly, and it is not repeated numerically in this vignette’s figure or tables.

What to read next

A quorum of lenses on Study A0 applies the front door to 200 recorded decision cells and generalises the two-lens cascade this vignette’s quorum() call is a miniature of. Getting started with quorum introduces the three on-ramps – ensemble ingestion, surrogate emulation, and the koine fourth opinion – that turn a non-hub estimate into a lens without writing an adapter like the one built here.

Reproduce

Seed 20260902 for the synthetic toy; seed = 1L inside lens_tmb()’s default and passed explicitly to flexyBayes::flexybayes(). Package versions follow.
